messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Dedicated pool 'horizon-enterprise-pool' (tenant=HorizonCorp) GPU queueing critical. queue_len=423 (threshold=200), gpu_util_avg=98%, kv_cache_miss=38%, error_rate(5xx)=2.7%. Paging on-call SREs. :rotating_light:
ryan-sre: ack. I'm up. grabbing dashboards and logs now. @pia-oncall-ml can you check model-level hotshards and KV usage?
pia-oncall-ml: looking. top offender is /v1/generate rt-gen-100 (long sequences, avg 5k tokens). KV cache occupancy for HorizonCorp is 78% of pool cache. Long completions causing high KV retention and preventing other requests from being scheduled.
tess-ops: pulling prometheus panels. pool=horizon-enterprise-pool -> GPUs_total=25, GPUs_used=24, pending_requests=423, avg_wait_ms=2800. autoscale config: min=25 max=25 (reserved-only). burst_enabled=false in pool config.
maria-cs: HorizonCorp CS says they're getting 503s and customer impact is urgent — they launched a campaign this morning. They want immediate mitigation.
devaditya: we have a couple of levers: temporary burst from global overflow, apply request-level throttling (max_new_tokens), or evict lower-priority jobs. Which do we want?
ryan-sre: quick triage: priority = customer SLA and revenue. Options pros/cons: burst -> preserves SLA but costs and risk of noisy-neighbor to shared pools; throttle -> immediate but might break customer flows; evict -> risky for other tenants. I think approve a short burst + soft throttles. @tess-ops can you outline the burst API and governance?
tess-ops: burst API: POST /internal/pools/{pool}/burst_override 
Payload: {"duration_seconds":3600, "max_gpus":4, "approver":"oncall-sre"}
Note: needs 2 approvals for >4 gpus. Billing path will flag extra usage.
ops-runbook-bot: runbook match: dedicated_pool_exhaustion_v2 -> steps: confirm impact -> attempt request-level mitigations -> consider burst_override -> update incident ticket -> notify customer.
pia-oncall-ml: immediate mitigation we can do without infra changes: apply a request transform at edge to cap max_new_tokens=1024 for HorizonCorp and enable KV eviction for sessions older than 10m. This reduces long-tail cache growth. I can push a quick patch to the transform service.
ryan-sre: do it. Maria, please notify customer we are enacting short-term mitigations and may enable temporary burst if needed. Use conservative wording.
maria-cs: on it. Drafting: "We're seeing sustained high throughput in your dedicated pool causing intermittent 503s. We're applying a temporary request cap and may enable limited burst capacity to stabilize. We'll update within 15 minutes."
ryan-sre: I'm going to approve a 45m burst_override for 4 GPUs to unblock traffic while pia's patch lands. Approving as oncall lead.
ryan-sre: (command) ```bash
curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood/api/v1/pools/horizon-enterprise-pool/burst_override \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"duration_seconds":2700, "max_gpus":4, "approver":"ryan-sre","reason":"HorizonCorp production spike - emergency burst"}'
```
ops-runbook-bot: approval recorded: approver=ryan-sre, gpus_granted=4, duration=2700s. Billing alert will be generated.
tess-ops: burst applied. system reports +3 GPUs assigned from overflow pool -> GPUs_used now 27 (overcommit allowed), pending_requests dropped from 423 -> 78 in ~2m. avg_wait_ms -> 620.
pia-oncall-ml: patch pushed to request-transform service to cap max_new_tokens and evict old KV keys. Config snippet:
```json
{"tenant":"HorizonCorp","transforms":[{"type":"set_max_new_tokens","value":1024},{"type":"kv_eviction","older_than_secs":600}]}
```
patch result: transform active on all edge nodes. observing drop in KV retention within 90s.
ryan-sre: monitoring. error_rate 5xx trending down 2.7% -> 0.4% after burst + transform. Queue_len trending down to 40. Good.
maria-cs: Customer update: "Thanks — we're seeing requests succeed again. Please keep us posted on any billing impacts."
devaditya: note: autoscale policy is fixed for this pool (reserved commit). We should file an action to revisit: add emergency-burst window or configurable burst budget for enterprise tenants. Also add per-tenant concurrency caps configurable by CS/SE.
ryan-sre: agreed. Action items: (1) Incident ticket INC-2026-3134567890 created (owner: ryan-sre) (2) Follow-up task for product: scoped autoscale/burst policy for reserved pools (owner: devaditya) (3) Cost review with finance for burst costs (owner: tess-ops) (4) RCA due EOD tomorrow.
ops-runbook-bot: close path: stabilize -> done. Please add postmortem label when incident signal fully cleared.
ryan-sre: handing off to night oncall @pia-oncall-ml for monitoring and customer follow-ups. I'm signing out in 10.
pia-oncall-ml: taking over. I'll keep watch for 2 hours and escalate if backlog >100 or error_rate >1%.
maria-cs: closing loop with HorizonCorp; they've paused the internal campaign to smooth traffic spikes. They requested an estimate of burst spend — tagging finance.
ryan-sre: final note: do not autoscale pool max beyond committed GPU count without product approval. This was an emergency, approved by oncall. Documenting in ticket.
ops-runbook-bot: incident status -> mitigated. Next steps: postmortem, plan for autoscale policy changes, improvements to request transforms, add detection rule for KV-cache-induced queueing. :white_check_mark:
